issue.title: SelfBuilding factory is bypassed after a previous resolution throws an exception
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.x-dev (`cdbd17f7e3257e8ae4207d3c3bef6058452d5f72`)

### PHP Version

8.5.10

### Database Driver & Version

N/A

### Description

When a `SelfBuilding::newInstance()` factory throws an exception, the container retains the class in its `buildStack`. A subsequent resolution of the same class through the same container skips the factory and constructs the object directly.

This can bypass validation or initialization performed by the factory. The existing `AolInstantMessengerConfig` integration-test fixture demonstrates the problem: its factory rejects an away-message duration below 60, but after the first `ValidationException`, a second resolution returns an object with duration 5.

Expected behavior: each independent resolution should invoke the factory and reject the invalid configuration. The factory's intentional recursive `app()->build(static::class)` call should continue to work while the factory is active.

The stack entry is added by `Container::buildSelfBuildingInstance()`, but its `array_pop()` only runs when the factory returns normally. The nested `Container::call()` does not own this entry because the class is already on the stack.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use the framework checkout at the commit above with its development dependencies installed.
2. Open [tests/Integration/Container/BuildableIntegrationTest.php](https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/cdbd17f7e3257e8ae4207d3c3bef6058452d5f72/tests/Integration/Container/BuildableIntegrationTest.php).
3. In `test_build_method_can_resolve_itself_via_container()`, preserve the initial valid configuration and assertions. Replace the final single `try/catch` with the following loop, keeping the existing `config(['aim.away_message.duration' => 5]);` immediately before it:

```php
for ($attempt = 1; $attempt <= 2; $attempt++) {
    try {
        $this->app->make(AolInstantMessengerConfig::class);

        $this->fail("Expected a validation exception on attempt {$attempt}.");
    } catch (ValidationException $exception) {
        $this->assertArrayHasKey('away_message.duration', $exception->errors());
        $this->assertStringContainsString('60', $exception->errors()['away_message.duration'][0]);
    }
}
```

4. Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Integration/Container/BuildableIntegrationTest.php --filter test_build_method_can_resolve_itself_via_container
```

The two attempts use the same application/container, without flushing or recreating it.

**Actual result:** the first attempt throws the expected `ValidationException`; the second returns normally and the test fails with:

```text
Expected a validation exception on attempt 2.
```

**Expected result:** both attempts throw `ValidationException`.

I reproduced this failure before changing production code. Locally, putting the factory call inside `try` and moving its stack cleanup into `finally` makes the regression pass. The expanded test also verifies recovery on the same container after setting duration to 60 and body to `back online`, using the fixture's existing recursive build path.

issue.title: LazyCollection::take() returns wrong items for a negative limit larger than the collection
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.31.0

### PHP Version

8.4.25

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

`take()` with a negative limit returns the last `$limit` items. When the collection holds fewer items than the limit, `Collection` returns the whole collection, but `LazyCollection` returns a `null` entry, drops real items, and emits warnings from inside the framework.

```php
(new Collection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all();     // ['a', 'b', 'c']
(new LazyCollection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all(); // ['' => null, 0 => 'a']
```

```
Warning: Undefined array key 3 in .../Illuminate/Collections/LazyCollection.php on line 1577
Warning: Trying to access array offset on null in .../Illuminate/Collections/LazyCollection.php on line 1577
```

The two classes implement the same `Enumerable` contract, so swapping one for the other silently changes the result here.

This only happens when `abs($limit)` is greater than the number of items. Every combination where `abs($limit) <= count()` agrees between the two classes, which is why the existing `testTakeLast` case (`take(-2)` on three items) does not catch it.

For reference, the results across sizes and limits, `Collection` first:

| items | limit | `Collection` | `LazyCollection` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | -2 | `['a']` | `['' => null]` |
| 2 | -3 | `['a', 'b']` | `['' => null, 0 => 'a']` |
| 3 | -5 | `['a', 'b', 'c']` | `['' => null, 0 => 'a']` |
| 4 | -5 | `['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']` | `['' => null, 0 => 'a', 1 => 'b', 2 => 'c']` |
| 5 | -7 | `['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e']` | `['' => null, 0 => 'a', 1 => 'b', 2 => 'c']` |

### Steps To Reproduce

```
composer require illuminate/collections
```

```php
<?php

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\LazyCollection;

var_dump((new Collection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all());
var_dump((new LazyCollection(['a', 'b', 'c']))->take(-5)->all());
```

Expected: both return `['a', 'b', 'c']`.

Actual: the `LazyCollection` call emits four warnings and returns `['' => null, 0 => 'a']`.

A fix was proposed in #61489.

issue.title: Auth::guard('sanctum')->user() returns the wrong user
TypeError in SessionGuard::userFromRecaller() when getAuthPassword() is null (passwordless apps)
issue.body:
**Laravel Version:** 13.31.0 (`12.x` is affected identically — see History)

**PHP Version:** 8.5.4

**Database Driver & Version:** MySQL 8.4.11

### Description

`SessionGuard::userFromRecaller()` throws a `TypeError` — a 500 on every request — when the user matched by the remember-me cookie has a null auth password:

```
TypeError: hash_equals(): Argument #1 ($known_string) must be of type string, null given
  at vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Auth/SessionGuard.php:239
#0 SessionGuard.php(239): hash_equals()
#1 SessionGuard.php(197): Illuminate\Auth\SessionGuard->userFromRecaller()
#2 AuthManager.php(61): Illuminate\Auth\SessionGuard->user()
#3 AuthServiceProvider.php(89): call_user_func()
#4 Request.php(677): call_user_func()
```

The code, identical in `12.x` and `13.x`:

```php
$userPassword = $user->getAuthPassword();

$recallerHash = $recaller->hash();

return (hash_equals($this->hashPasswordForCookie($userPassword), $recallerHash)
        || hash_equals($userPassword, $recallerHash))
    ? $user : null;
```

We run a passwordless application — login is OTP and passkey only, and the `users` table has no `password` column at all — so `getAuthPassword()` returns `null` for every user. After upgrading from 13.26.1 to 13.30.1, every user holding a remember-me cookie got a 500 on their first request once the session expired: home page, login page, every route. It keeps happening on each request until the cookie expires or the user clears it, and since the crash happens while resolving the user, there is no logout path to recover from it in the browser.

Two separate things go wrong:

1. `hashPasswordForCookie(null)` calls `hash_hmac('sha256', null, ...)`, which raises `Deprecated: hash_hmac(): Passing null to parameter #2 ($data) of type string is deprecated` and returns the HMAC of the empty string. So the first comparison silently compares against the wrong value.
2. The second `hash_equals($userPassword, $recallerHash)` then gets the raw `null` and throws.

Cookies issued before #61386 store the auth password itself as the third segment, which for these users is an empty string. `Recaller::hasAllSegments()` only requires the first two segments to be non-empty, so such a cookie passes `valid()` and reaches the comparison.

Worth noting that the deprecation in (1) also fires on the **write** path: `queueRecallerCookie()` calls `hashPasswordForCookie($user->getAuthPassword())`, so the framework itself feeds a null to `hash_hmac()` when issuing the cookie. Under PHP 9 that stops being a deprecation.

### Why this reads as a bug rather than a misconfiguration

A null auth password is treated as a supported state everywhere else in the same component:

- `EloquentUserProvider::validateCredentials()` — `if (is_null($hashed = $user->getAuthPassword())) { return false; }`
- `DatabaseUserProvider::validateCredentials()` — identical guard
- `Illuminate\Session\Middleware\AuthenticateSession::handle()` — `if (! $request->hasSession() || ! $request->user() || ! $request->user()->getAuthPassword()) { return $next($request); }`

`userFromRecaller()` is now the only place in the auth stack that assumes a string.

### History

- #61386 added the password-hash check to `userFromRecaller()` in `12.x`.
- #61396 reported a `TypeError` on the *no matching user* path; fixed by #61397 with `if (! $this->viaRemember) { return; }`. That guard is present in 13.30.1+.
- #61433 proposed the fix for this *no password* path and was closed without comment on 2026-09-04.

Both `12.x` and `13.x` still carry the unguarded code as of today, and the change reached `13.x` through commit `3005430` ("port fixes from 12.x"), released in v13.30.1 — which is not mentioned in that release's notes, so there was nothing to react to at upgrade time.

### What I am actually asking

If a null `getAuthPassword()` is no longer supported, that is a perfectly reasonable answer — but then it is a behavioural break that deserves a line in the upgrade guide, and the three null-guards listed above are dead code that suggests the opposite. If it is still supported, `userFromRecaller()` needs the guard that `AuthenticateSession` already has. Either way, an application should not be able to 500 itself on every route with a cookie the framework issued.

### Steps To Reproduce

On a fresh application:

1. Make `users.password` nullable, or remove the column so `getAuthPassword()` returns null.
2. While on 13.29.0 (or 12.68), call `Auth::login($user, remember: true)`. Equivalently, hand-craft the cookie value as `{id}|{remember_token}|` — an empty third segment is what these users get.
3. Upgrade to 13.30.1 or later (12.69 or later on `12.x`).
4. Delete the session cookie, keep `remember_web_*`, and request any route that resolves the user.

Every request returns 500 until the cookie is gone. On 13.29.0 the same cookie logs the user in.

### Workaround

For anyone who lands here from a search, on the application side:

```php
// app/Models/User.php
public function getAuthPassword(): string
{
    return '';
}
```

Existing cookies keep working — the empty third segment matches on the second comparison, new ones match on the first — and `AuthenticateSession` still skips its check. The remember token itself is still verified by `retrieveByToken()`, so a forged cookie still resolves to a guest.

issue.title: resolveClassAttribute() cache key omits $property, so #[Table(timestamps:)] collides with isIgnoringTouch()
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.20.0

### PHP Version

8.5.8

### Database Driver & Version

_Not applicable — reproduces without a database connection._

### Description

`Model::resolveClassAttribute()` builds its cache key from the class and the attribute class only:

```php
// Illuminate/Database/Eloquent/Model.php:2681
$cacheKey = $class.'@'.$attributeClass;
```

but when `$property` is passed it stores the **property value** under that same key:

```php
// Illuminate/Database/Eloquent/Model.php:2696
return static::$classAttributes[$cacheKey] = $property ? $instance->{$property} : $instance;
```

`$property` is not part of the key, so the 2-arg and 3-arg forms share one cache slot. For `Table::class` both forms are live:

- `Model::initializeModelAttributes()` (Model.php:436) — `resolveClassAttribute(Table::class)`, expects the **object**
- `HasTimestamps::initializeHasTimestamps()` (HasTimestamps.php:38) — `resolveClassAttribute(Table::class)`, expects the **object**
- `Model::isIgnoringTouch()` (Model.php:545) — `resolveClassAttribute(Table::class, 'timestamps', $class)`, expects **?bool**

Whichever runs first poisons the other, and it breaks in both directions.

### Steps To Reproduce

```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Table;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

#[Table(name: 't', timestamps: false)] class Z1 extends Model {}
#[Table(name: 't', timestamps: false)] class Z2 extends Model {}

// A) construct first (what the framework normally does) -> the Table OBJECT is cached.
new Z1();
var_dump(Z1::isIgnoringTouch());   // false  — expected true

// B) isIgnoringTouch() first on a cold cache -> the BOOL is cached, poisoning construction.
var_dump(Z2::isIgnoringTouch());   // true
$z2 = new Z2();
var_dump($z2->usesTimestamps());   // true    — expected false, #[Table(timestamps:)] ignored
var_dump($z2->getTable());         // 'z2_s'  — expected 't',   #[Table(name:)] ignored
```

`isIgnoringTouch()` is a `protected static`; in A it is reachable through `Relation::touch()` (Relation.php:224) and `BelongsToMany` (BelongsToMany.php:1318), both of which hold an already-constructed instance — so **A is the order that occurs in normal use**.

In A, `isIgnoringTouch()` reads a cached `Table` object where it expects `?bool`. The object is truthy, so `! $timestamps` is false and it returns `false`: a model that declared `#[Table(timestamps: false)]` still gets touched by its relations.

In B, the cached `bool` is handed back to `initializeModelAttributes()` and `initializeHasTimestamps()`, which expect a `Table`, and **both `#[Table]` arguments are silently dropped** — the model keeps the derived table name and stays timestamped.

### Expected

`#[Table(timestamps: false)]` disables timestamps and suppresses touches; `#[Table(name: 't')]` sets the table. Neither should depend on which method warmed the cache first.

### Possible fix

Include `$property` in the key, so the two forms cannot share a slot:

```php
$cacheKey = $class.'@'.$attributeClass.'@'.$property;
```

Found while implementing a mirror of `initializeHasTimestamps()` in a static-analysis tool ([psalm-plugin-laravel#1276](https://github.com/psalm/psalm-plugin-laravel/issues/1276)); the plugin resolves attributes uncached, which is what surfaced the divergence.

issue.title: Redis tagged cache: entries written concurrently with flush() are never invalidated again
DB connection refused (ECONNREFUSED) causes unbounded memory growth instead of QueryException since v13.21.0
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.21.0 through 13.35.0 (confirmed still present at 13.35.0, the latest at time of writing). Not present in 13.20.0 or earlier.

### PHP Version

8.3.33

### Database Driver & Version

PostgreSQL (`pdo_pgsql`), but the failure is in `Illuminate\Database\Connectors\Connector` / `Illuminate\Database\Connection`, not in the pgsql-specific driver code, so it may well reproduce on other drivers.

### Description

When a connection attempt is refused (nothing listening on the target host/port), the connector's reconnect-on-lost-connection path no longer fails fast with a `QueryException`. Instead the PHP process's memory grows until it hits `memory_limit` and dies with a fatal error, e.g.:

```
PHP Fatal error:  Allowed memory size of 536870912 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 20480 bytes) in vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php on line 857
```

(The exact line/file varies slightly by patch version — sometimes `Illuminate/Database/Connectors/Connector.php`, sometimes `Illuminate/Database/Connection.php` — but the symptom is the same runaway memory growth instead of a clean exception.)

This is a real regression for anything that relies on a failed DB connection surfacing as a catchable exception rather than crashing the worker — for example a health-check endpoint (`/up`) that is supposed to keep answering even while the database is down, or any test suite asserting that behavior.

I bisected it with `composer require laravel/framework:<version> --with-all-dependencies --no-interaction` between a known-good and known-bad version:

| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| 13.20.0 | OK — throws `Illuminate\Database\QueryException` immediately |
| 13.21.0 | **Fails** — fatal error, memory exhausted |
| 13.22.0, 13.24.0, 13.28.0, 13.35.0 | **Fails** — same symptom |

So the regression was introduced specifically between `v13.20.0` and `v13.21.0`.

### Steps To Reproduce

Minimal repro, run from the root of any Laravel app with Postgres support installed (`php artisan tinker` or a one-off script bootstrapping the app):

```php
config(['database.connections.unreachable' => [
    'driver' => 'pgsql',
    'host' => '127.0.0.1',
    'port' => 1, // nothing listens here — connection refused immediately
    'database' => 'whatever',
    'username' => 'whatever',
    'password' => 'whatever',
]]);

DB::purge('unreachable');

DB::connection('unreachable')->select('select 1');
```

Expected: throws `Illuminate\Database\QueryException` (SQLSTATE[08006], connection refused), as it does on `13.20.0` and earlier.

Actual (13.21.0+): the PHP process's memory grows until `memory_limit` is hit and the process dies with a fatal error instead of the query ever raising a catchable exception.

issue.title: JsonApiResource loads relationships one model at a time, so ?include= on a collection costs a query per record
issue.body:
- Laravel version: 13.24.0
- PHP version: 8.5.9
- Database driver & version: SQLite 3 in memory, through Testbench 11.1

I was counting queries on an ordinary index endpoint and ended up with 101
queries for 100 records with ?include=comments. The same listing built as
Post::with('comments')->get() gives 2. Before I read anything into that I'd
like to know whether the loading is meant to be the developer's job here.

Where it comes from, as far as I can tell. ResolvesJsonApiElements::
compileResourceRelationships() calls $this->resource->loadMissing(...), and
$this->resource in that method is always a single model, because both callers
return early unless it is one. AnonymousResourceCollection::toAttributes()
then maps resolveResourceData() over the collection item by item, so every
item runs its own loadMissing against its own model.

The nested level behaves differently, and that's why I'm asking rather than
just eager loading and moving on. With 10 posts and
?include=comments.author I get 21 queries: one for the posts, ten for the
comments, ten for the authors. But the author lookups are batched inside each
post, select * from "authors" where "authors"."id" in (1, 2, 3), because the
second loadMissing runs on $relatedModels, which is already a collection. So
the batching is there. It just never reaches the outer level.

What I measured, all on 13.24.0:

| request                                   | queries |
|-------------------------------------------|---------|
| single post, ?include=comments            | 2       |
| 10 posts, no eager loading                | 11      |
| 10 posts, with('comments')                | 2       |
| 10 posts, ?include=comments.author        | 21      |
| 10 posts, with('comments.author')         | 3       |
| 100 posts, no eager loading               | 101     |
| 100 posts, with('comments')               | 2       |

I'm leaving timings out on purpose. This is sqlite in memory, so the numbers
there say more about serialisation than about the database, and the counts
are what matters.

The case for "working as intended", which I can make myself: the call is
loadMissing and not load, which reads like topping up whatever the developer
forgot, not like owning the loading, and the documentation does show eager
loading in the controller. If that's the answer then this is a documentation
note at most and I'll drop it. It just seems like a lot to leave to a query
log on an endpoint whose output is completely correct.

Two things I did not check, in case they matter: whether the same happens
through an explicit ResourceCollection class and not the anonymous one, and
whether chaperone() changes any of it. Both looked like separate paths
when I skimmed them, so I might be missing something.

Steps to reproduce

Post hasMany Comment, Comment belongsTo Author. Resources generated with
make:resource --json-api, PostResource declaring $relationships = ['comments'],
CommentResource declaring $relationships = ['author'].

Route returning PostResource::collection(Post::all()), 100 posts with three
comments each, then GET /posts?include=comments with
Accept: application/vnd.api+json and DB::listen() counting.

issue.title: Numeric rules throw uncaught Brick NumberFormatException for is_numeric-accepted strings trim() does not clean (e.g. "\x0C5")
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.24.0 (code verified unchanged at v13.26.1 and current `13.x` head)

### PHP Version

8.5.9

### Database Driver & Version

n/a (no database involved)

### Description

Every numeric comparison rule (`min`, `max`, `size`, `between`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`) can throw an **uncaught** `Brick\Math\Exception\NumberFormatException` instead of failing validation, when the value is a string that `is_numeric()` accepts but PHP's `trim()` does not clean — for example a form feed (`\x0C`) adjacent to a digit. In an HTTP context this surfaces as a 500 for input that should simply produce a validation message.

The mechanism, with line references to `src/Illuminate/Validation/Concerns/ValidatesAttributes.php` at v13.26.1:

- `is_numeric("\x0C5")` is `true` (PHP counts `\x0C` as leading whitespace for `is_numeric`), so `getSize()` takes its numeric branch.
- `getSize()` takes its numeric branch and returns the value through `$this->trim($value)`.
- `$this->trim($value)` uses PHP `trim()`, whose default charlist (`" \t\n\r\0\x0B"`) does **not** include `\x0C`, so the form feed survives.
- `BigNumber::of("\x0C5")` (e.g. `validateMax()`, line 1711) throws `Brick\Math\Exception\NumberFormatException: Value "5" does not represent a valid number.`
- The surrounding `catch (MathException)` (line 1712) refers to `Illuminate\Support\Exceptions\MathException` (imported at line 22). Brick's exceptions implement `Brick\Math\Exception\MathException` — a different, unrelated type (imported at line 7 as `BrickMathException`) — so nothing catches the throw. The only rule that catches the Brick type is `validateMultipleOf()` (line 1976).

Notes:

- Over HTTP with the default global middleware, `TrimStrings` (via `Str::trim`, whose `\s`-based regex does strip `\x0C`) removes *leading/trailing* form feeds, which masks the simplest case. The crash remains reachable wherever the validator runs on input that middleware did not clean: direct `Validator::make()` usage, queued/imported data, custom pipelines, or apps that exclude/replace `TrimStrings`.
- `\x0C` is the clearest trigger because it is the one byte `is_numeric()` accepts as padding that `trim()` does not strip. The class of bug is the type mismatch in the `catch`, so any future `BigNumber::of` failure mode lands the same way — #55944, #46225, #59555, #59559 and #60697 were earlier reports/proposals in this same class.

The natural fix is to widen the catches to `catch (MathException|BrickMathException)` — the shape `validateMultipleOf()` already uses in this same trait (and which #59559 proposed for a related trigger). Unlike the earlier INF/NAN reports, the trigger here is an ordinary request string, not a special float value.

Found while hardening input handling in an application; happy to PR either direction if the maintainers indicate a preference.

### Steps To Reproduce

Standalone, no app required:

```php
<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use Illuminate\Translation\{ArrayLoader, Translator};
use Illuminate\Validation\Factory;

$factory = new Factory(new Translator(new ArrayLoader(), 'en'));

// Expected: fails() === true with the numeric message.
// Actual:   uncaught Brick\Math\Exception\NumberFormatException:
//           Value "5" does not represent a valid number.
$factory->make(['n' => "\x0C5"], ['n' => 'numeric|max:10'])->fails();
```

`"5\x0C"` (trailing form feed) throws identically. `"\x0C"` alone fails cleanly (correct), because `is_numeric` rejects it.

issue.title: A failed COMMIT leaves the transaction pending in DatabaseTransactionsManager: afterCommit callbacks hang or run twice
Facades and the container instance point to different applications after route:cache
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.30.0 and 13.30.1 (13.29.0 is fine)

### PHP Version

8.5.10 (also 8.5.9)

### Database Driver & Version

Not involved. Reproduced on the default SQLite of a fresh install and on PostgreSQL 17.

### Description

Since #61346 (13.30.0) `RouteCacheCommand::getFreshApplication()` boots a throwaway `Application` and afterwards restores the facade root to the live application:

```php
Facade::clearResolvedInstances();
Facade::setFacadeApplication($this->laravel);
```

`new Application` also calls `Container::setInstance($this)` (in `registerBaseBindings()`), and nothing restores that. So after `route:cache` the process is in a split state: facades resolve against the live app, while `Container::getInstance()` / `app()` resolve against the discarded one. Before 13.30 both pointed at the throwaway app, which was equally wrong but self-consistent, so it never showed.

`optimize` runs `view:cache` right after `route:cache` in the same process, and `view:cache` falls into the split:

1. `ViewClearCommand` / `ViewCacheCommand` resolve the Blade engine through `$this->laravel['view.engine.resolver']->resolve('blade')`, i.e. on the live app.
2. The `blade` engine closure in `ViewServiceProvider::registerBladeEngine()` builds the engine from `Container::getInstance()->make('blade.compiler')`, i.e. the throwaway app's compiler.
3. That resolution fires the `afterResolving('blade.compiler')` hooks. A package that registers class component namespaces there through the `Blade` facade (inertia-laravel 3.x does: `Blade::componentNamespace('Inertia\\View\\Components', 'inertia')`) registers them on the live app's compiler instead.
4. The compiler that actually compiles has an empty `classComponentNamespaces`, and the first `<x-inertia::...>` tag fails:

```
  views .......................................................... 9.32ms FAIL

In ComponentTagCompiler.php line 315:

  Unable to locate a class or view for component [inertia::head].
```

`php artisan view:cache` on its own succeeds (no `route:cache` ran before it in that process). 13.29.0 succeeds. 13.30.x with `getFreshApplication()` reverted to the 13.29 body succeeds.

Instrumented run on 13.30.0 (ids from `spl_object_id`; `#4` is the live app, `#2531` the throwaway app booted by `route:cache`):

```
inertia callback:           providerApp#2531 passedCompiler#4100 facadeApp#4 facadeCompiler#4463
componentClass(inertia::app): compiler#4100 namespaces=[] facadeApp#4 container#2531
```

The namespace went to compiler #4463, the compilation ran on #4100.

Inertia could dodge this particular symptom by using the compiler instance passed to its callback instead of the facade (reported separately to inertiajs/inertia-laravel), but the split between `Facade::getFacadeApplication()` and `Container::getInstance()` is in the framework and affects anything that runs after `route:cache` in the same process and goes through `app()` / `Container::getInstance()`.

### Steps To Reproduce

```sh
composer create-project laravel/laravel repro        # 13.30.1
cd repro
composer require inertiajs/inertia-laravel           # 3.3.1
cat > resources/views/app.blade.php <<'BLADE'
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head><x-inertia::head /></head>
<body><x-inertia::app /></body>
</html>
BLADE

php artisan optimize        # views FAIL: Unable to locate a class or view for component [inertia::head]
php artisan optimize:clear
php artisan view:cache      # OK

composer require laravel/framework:13.29.0 -W
php artisan optimize        # config / events / routes / views all DONE
```

### Suggested fix

Restore the container instance together with the facade root:

```php
protected function getFreshApplication()
{
    return tap(require $this->laravel->bootstrapPath('app.php'), function ($app) {
        $app->make(ConsoleKernelContract::class)->bootstrap();

        Facade::clearResolvedInstances();
        Facade::setFacadeApplication($this->laravel);
        Container::setInstance($this->laravel);
    });
}
```

`ConfigCacheCommand::getFreshConfiguration()` boots a throwaway app the same way and leaves `Container::getInstance()` on it too; #61350 / #61351 proposed the facade-only restore for it, so whatever lands there should keep the two in sync as well.

Workarounds until then: run `config:cache`, `event:cache`, `route:cache`, `view:cache` as separate processes instead of `optimize`, or pin `laravel/framework:13.29.0`.

issue.title: CloudBootstrapper renumbers pgsql PDO options for -pooler hosts (array_merge on int keys)
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.31.0 (same code on the current 13.x branch)

### PHP Version

8.4.25

### Database Driver & Version

pgsql, Laravel Cloud Serverless Postgres through the `-pooler` endpoint

### Description

When `database.connections.pgsql.host` contains `pg.laravel.cloud` and `-pooler`, `CloudBootstrapper::configureUnpooledPostgresConnection()` adds emulated prepares like this:

```php
$app['config']->set(
    'database.connections.pgsql.options',
    array_merge(
        $app['config']->get('database.connections.pgsql.options', []),
        [PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true],
    ),
);
```

PDO attribute keys are integers, and `array_merge()` renumbers integer keys. Any PDO options the app already set are therefore re-keyed from 0 and applied to the wrong attributes. For example:

```php
array_merge(
    [PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5, PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true, Pdo\Pgsql::ATTR_DISABLE_PREPARES => true],
    [PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true],
);
// [0 => 5, 1 => true, 2 => true, 3 => true]
// = ATTR_AUTOCOMMIT => 5, ATTR_PREFETCH => true, ATTR_TIMEOUT => 1, ATTR_ERRMODE => 1 (ERRMODE_WARNING)
```

Effects:

- `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES` itself is lost. So is any `ATTR_PERSISTENT` or `Pdo\Pgsql::ATTR_DISABLE_PREPARES` the app set.
- `ATTR_ERRMODE` becomes `ERRMODE_WARNING`. The key 3 value overrides the connector's default `ERRMODE_EXCEPTION`, so query errors surface as PHP warnings (`ErrorException`) instead of `QueryException`.
- The connect timeout becomes 1 second.

Because emulation is lost, pdo_pgsql uses named server-side prepared statements through the transaction pooler. With a libpq older than 17, pdo_pgsql frees statements with SQL `DEALLOCATE pdo_stmt_N`. PgBouncer (`max_prepared_statements` > 0) has renamed the statements to `PGBOUNCER_N`, so the `DEALLOCATE` fails with 26000. pdo_pgsql ignores that error, but the open transaction is aborted, and the next statement fails:

```
SQLSTATE[25P02]: In failed sql transaction: ERROR: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block
```

We hit this in `DB::transaction()` blocks with more than one query (a deploy seeder) right after switching `DB_HOST` to the `-pooler` endpoint.

The default `config/database.php` sets no pgsql `options`, so apps on the stock config are not affected. Any app that sets PDO options on pgsql is.

### Steps To Reproduce

```php
config([
    'database.connections.pgsql.host' => 'ep-example-123456-pooler.us-east-2.pg.laravel.cloud',
    'database.connections.pgsql.options' => [
        PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5,
        PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true,
    ],
]);

\Illuminate\Foundation\CloudBootstrapper::configureUnpooledPostgresConnection(app());

var_dump(config('database.connections.pgsql.options'));
// array(3) { [0]=> int(5) [1]=> bool(true) [2]=> bool(true) }
// expected: [PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 5, PDO::ATTR_PERSISTENT => true, PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => true]
```

End to end: a Laravel Cloud app whose pgsql connection sets any PDO options, `DB_HOST` pointed at the `-pooler` endpoint, and a `DB::transaction()` that runs two queries. It fails with 25P02 on the second query.

Suggested fix: assign the key instead of merging, for example `$app['config']->set('database.connections.pgsql.options.'.PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES, true)`, so existing integer keys are preserved and emulation is forced as intended.

issue.title: Http::retry() with attach(fopen()) drops the file, then throws InvalidArgumentException
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.32.0

### PHP Version

8.3.33

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

attach() accepts a stream resource, and the docs show fopen() as a normal way to upload:

https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/http-client#multi-part-requests

retry() says that exhausting a connection failure throws Illuminate\Http\Client\ConnectionException:

https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/http-client#retries

With a real fopen() handle, those two do not combine.

PendingRequest::send() builds the multipart options once, before the retry loop, and every attempt reuses that same resource. Reproduced on Laravel 13.32.0 (PHP 8.3.33, Guzzle 7.15.5, guzzlehttp/psr7 2.13.1) with retry(3) against a refused port:

- Attempt 1 sends the file bytes, then fails to connect.
- Attempt 2 sends again, but the handle is already at EOF, so the part does not contain the file.
- Attempt 3 throws InvalidArgumentException: Invalid resource type: resource (closed).

Passing file_get_contents() instead keeps the bytes on every attempt, and the final exception is a ConnectionException.

retry(2) hides the exception: the second attempt still fails to connect, so the caller sees only ConnectionException, even though the file bytes were already missing from that attempt.

### Steps To Reproduce

$path = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), 'upload');
file_put_contents($path, 'hello-stream');

Http::retry(3, 0)
    ->connectTimeout(1)
    ->timeout(1)
    ->attach('file', fopen($path, 'rb'), 'hello.txt')
    ->post('http://127.0.0.1:1/upload');

issue.title: Changes to ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing in #59567 causing lost jobs in 13.5.0
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.5.0

### PHP Version

8.5

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

Changes to `ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing` in #59567 are causing what appears to be lost jobs in 13.5.0.
 
### Scenario

I have a production Laravel application that uses jobs heavily. It's been working properly for >1 year, through many framework upgrades, but started failing after upgrading to 13.5.0 with what appears to be lost jobs.

I have a model with a `stale_since` timestamp. When something changes the model, I set the model's `stale_since` to the current date and dispatch a job, which performs some calculations and clears `stale_since`. The job has `ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing` and `WithoutOverlapping` middleware, so there should be at most 2 instances of the job for a given model at a given point in time - 0..1 pending and 0..1 processing. A job dispatched after setting `stale_since` may ultimately not be run - it may be dropped by `ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing` because another job is pending for that model - but in that case the pending job should ultimately clear the model's `stale_since`.

(I'm aware there are at least 2 logical race conditions in what I'm describing. This is an oversimplification. All that matters is that the the final `stale_since` that gets set should be cleared by the final job that gets processed, even if that job was already pending when the final `stale_since` was set. 😄)

In 13.4.0 and earlier, this logic held. 

However, after upgrading to 13.5.0, I've suddenly started seeing models with `stale_since` set long after they should have been cleared, with no jobs pending, and with no exceptions and no failed jobs logged. It seems the jobs were "lost" in the framework. 

Downgrading to 13.4.0 immediately resolved the issue.

Patching 13.5.0 to revert #59567 also resolved the issue.

### Steps To Reproduce

I've created a self-contained repro that sets up this exact scenario as simply as I can. It passes with 13.4.0, fails with 13.5.0, and passes with 13.5.0 patched to revert #59567:

https://github.com/nmbrcolin/repro-stale

issue.title: TrustProxies with at: * does not work correctly when request has passed through multiple proxies
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

12.63.0, 13.x

### PHP Version

8.4

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

I have an application running on ELB behind a CloudFront distribution. Both ELB and CloudFront forward the request downstream resulting in my X-Forwarded-For header looking like this:

`1.1.1.1, 2.2.2.2`

Where `1.1.1.1` is my actual client IP address, 2.2.2.2 is CloudFront, and 3.3.3.3 is ELB.

I have trusted all proxies with the line:
```
$middleware->trustProxies(
            at: '*',
            headers: Request::HEADER_X_FORWARDED_FOR |
            Request::HEADER_X_FORWARDED_HOST |
            Request::HEADER_X_FORWARDED_PORT |
            Request::HEADER_X_FORWARDED_PROTO |
            Request::HEADER_X_FORWARDED_AWS_ELB
        );
```

However when I call `$request->ip()` I get `2.2.2.2`

I've dug into this a bit and discovered this is because when Laravel trusts all proxies, it sets the list of trusted IPs to the REMOTE_ADDR (3.3.3.3 in my case). 
This list ends up getting passed to Symfony, which then returns the latest untrusted IP in the list, which is `2.2.2.2`.

As Symfony does not support wildcards, my proposed fix for this is to set the trusted proxies to 0 netmasks (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0), so that Symfony trusts the entire chain and will therefore return the first trusted IP, 1.1.1.1 in my case.

I note that there is a test case for this but it appears to be incorrect, according to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Forwarded-For the leftmost IP is the original client IP, which reflects in what I am seeing.

I have a fix in progress for this, will raise a PR

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start a Laravel app with TrustProxies:* 
2. Craft a request with multiple IP addresses in X-FORWARDED-FOR or FORWARDED header
3. Observe that the last IP in the list is used as the original client IP, not the first!

issue.title: [PHPLARA-311] `queue:retry all` throws TypeError with the documented failed-job config on 5.x (`ids()` returns ObjectId)
issue.body:
- Laravel-mongodb Version: 5.11.0 - PHP Version: 8.4.26 - Database Driver & Version: ext-mongodb 2.5.3, mongodb/mongodb 2.4.2, MongoDB server 8.0 (Laravel framework 13.34.0) ### Description: `php artisan queue:retry all` (and `queue:retry --queue=`) throws a `TypeError` as soon as at least one failed job is stored in MongoDB. This happens with the failed-job configuration shown in the [Queues documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/php/laravel-mongodb/current/queues/) (`'driver' => 'mongodb'`) and also with `'driver' => 'database'`. In both cases Laravel resolves `Illuminate\Queue\Failed\DatabaseFailedJobProvider`. This is the minimal 5.x reproduction requested in #3000. **Why it happens:** 1. `DatabaseFailedJobProvider::ids()` returns `$this->getTable()->orderBy('id', 'desc')->pluck('id')->all()`. 2. With the 5.x query builder, `_id` is aliased to `id`, but the value stays a `MongoDB\BSON\ObjectId` instance. 3. `RetryCommand::handle()` wraps each result with `new Collection([$id => $found])`. An `ObjectId` cannot be an array key, so PHP throws. Retrying explicit ids (`queue:retry 6ac3...`) works, because those ids are strings and `find()` / `forget()` convert them back to `ObjectId`. **Background:** - [PHPORM-167](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/PHPORM-167) fixed this exact command in 4.3 by adding `MongoFailedJobProvider::ids()`. - [PHPORM-231](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/PHPORM-231) removed `MongoFailedJobProvider` in 5.0, on the basis that `DatabaseFailedJobProvider` now works with the MongoDB query builder. - The `id`/`_id` aliasing covers the queries, but not the type of the id values that `ids()` returns. So the `queue:retry all` regression came back. Laravel's default failed driver, `database-uuids`, is **not** affected, because `ids()` plucks the string `uuid` column. However, the documented configuration and the plain `database` driver are affected. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a fresh app and install the package: ```bash composer create-project laravel/laravel app "^13.0" cd app composer require mongodb/laravel-mongodb:5.10.0 ``` 2. Add a MongoDB connection to `config/database.php`: ```php 'mongodb' => ['driver' => 'mongodb', 'dsn' => 'mongodb://localhost:27017', 'database' => 'repro'], ``` 3. Set `config/queue.php` as in the docs: ```php 'failed' => ['driver' => 'mongodb', 'database' => 'mongodb', 'table' => 'failed_jobs'], ``` 4. Store one failed job and retry it: ```bash php artisan tinker --execute='app("queue.failer")->log("database", "default", json_encode(["uuid" => (string) Str::uuid(), "displayName" => "X", "job" => "X", "data" => []]), new RuntimeException("boom")); var_dump(app("queue.failer")->ids());' php artisan queue:retry all ``` ### Expected behaviour `ids()` returns scalar ids. `queue:retry all` pushes the job back onto its queue and removes it from `failed_jobs`, the same as with the `database-uuids` driver. ### Actual behaviour `ids()` returns `ObjectId` instances. `queue:retry all` exits with code 1, and the failed job stays in the collection. ``` array(1) { [0] => class MongoDB\BSON\ObjectId#6567 (1) { public $oid => string(24) "6ac339e3d1d274e29d01e192" } } INFO Pushing failed queue jobs back onto the queue. TypeError Cannot access offset of type MongoDB\BSON\ObjectId on array at vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Queue/Console/RetryCommand.php:58 57▕ if (! $found instanceof Enumerable) { ➜ 58▕ $found = new Collection([$id => $found]); 59▕ } ``` In production this means a scheduled `queue:retry all` fails on every run once any job has failed, so no failed job is ever retried.
Workaround Decorate `queue.failer` and cast the ids to strings. ```php use Illuminate\Queue\Failed\DatabaseFailedJobProvider; class MongoFailedJobProvider extends DatabaseFailedJobProvider { public function ids($queue = null): array { return array_map(fn ($id) => (string) $id, parent::ids($queue)); } } // AppServiceProvider::register() // QueueServiceProvider is deferred: a singleton() binding would be overwritten when it loads, extend() is not. $this->app->extend('queue.failer', function ($failer, $app) { if (! $failer instanceof DatabaseFailedJobProvider) { return $failer; } $config = $app['config']['queue.failed']; return new MongoFailedJobProvider($app['db'], $config['database'], $config['table']); }); ``` Switching to `database-uuids` also avoids the crash. It only works when every failed payload contains a `uuid` key, though. That is not the case for raw messages consumed from external brokers: there, `log()` hits `Undefined array key "uuid"`.
### Possible fixes - Have the package decorate `queue.failer` (or register its own `mongodb` failed driver) so that `ids()` returns strings, or - document `database-uuids` as the recommended driver and the limitation of `mongodb` / `database`.

issue.title: `request()->clamp('my-var')` results in 500 if my-var is empty or string
Framework class-based casts handle JSON null differently than string-based casts
Database cache lock bug: SAVEPOINT trans2 does not exist
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.33.0

### PHP Version

8.5

### Database Driver & Version

MySQL 8 (InnoDB)

### Description

When inside of transaction you use cache lock, it doesn't handle correctly deadlock and swallows exception. Instead of stopping PHP code it allows it to execute further.
I am too stupid to explain in the the full detail. I will paste the AI explanation. 
Basically this problem happens for us in production when multiple users hit the same code.


### Steps To Reproduce

Text by AI:

`DatabaseLock::acquire()` catches any `QueryException` from its lock-table INSERT and tries an UPDATE. This includes MySQL deadlock error 1213, not just a duplicate-key error.

If the lock uses the same connection as an open application transaction, MySQL can roll back that entire transaction on a deadlock. Because the exception is caught, application code can continue while Laravel still reports an open transaction. Earlier writes are gone, later writes may autocommit, and a subsequent nested rollback can fail with `SAVEPOINT trans2 does not exist`.

Use MySQL/InnoDB with `DB_CONNECTION=mysql`, `CACHE_STORE=database`, migrated `cache` and `cache_locks` tables, and `lock_connection` unset. Open two fresh Tinker sessions. Use the same unused `$id` in both.

**Session A:**

```php
$id = 'deadlock-report-001';

DB::beginTransaction();

foreach (range(1, 20) as $i) {
    DB::table('cache')->insert([
        'key' => "filler-$id-$i",
        'value' => '1',
        'expiration' => time() + 600,
    ]);
}

Cache::store('database')->lock("foo-$id", 600)->get(); // true
```

**Session B:**

```php
$id = 'deadlock-report-001';

DB::beginTransaction();

DB::table('cache')->insert([
    'key' => "marker-$id",
    'value' => '1',
    'expiration' => time() + 600,
]);
```

**Back in A:** Run this; it should block waiting for B's uncommitted marker row.

```php
DB::table('cache')->where('key', "marker-$id")->delete();
```

**While A is blocked, in B:**

```php
Cache::store('database')->lock("foo-$id", 600)->get();
```

B now waits for A's lock, completing the deadlock cycle. The 20 filler rows make A the more expensive transaction to roll back, encouraging MySQL to choose B as the victim. Once A's delete unblocks, run `DB::rollBack()` **in A** so B's lock-acquisition fallback can finish.

**Inspect B:**

```php
DB::transactionLevel();                         // 1
DB::getPdo()->inTransaction();                   // false
DB::table('cache')->where('key', "marker-$id")->exists(); // false

DB::transaction(fn () => throw new RuntimeException('probe'));
// May report: SAVEPOINT trans2 does not exist
```

## Expected

The deadlock exception propagates; code does not continue under an invalid outer transaction.

## Actual

The lock INSERT's deadlock exception is caught. Laravel can report transaction level `1` after MySQL has rolled the transaction back.

This manual interleaving depends on MySQL choosing B as the deadlock victim. The important evidence is the `1`/`false` transaction-state mismatch; the savepoint error is a downstream symptom.

issue.title: number() prompt throws instead of falling back in non-interactive environments
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.x (2c410561c)

### PHP Version

8.5.9

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

`Laravel\Prompts\NumberPrompt` is the only prompt type that has no fallback registered in `Illuminate\Console\Concerns\ConfiguresPrompts`. Every other prompt (`text`, `textarea`, `password`, `pause`, `confirm`, `select`, `multiselect`, `suggest`, `search`, `multisearch`) registers one via `fallbackUsing()`.

Prompts fall back to plain Symfony console questions whenever `Prompt::fallbackWhen(windows_os() || $this->laravel->runningUnitTests())` is true — i.e. on Windows, in non-TTY/non-interactive contexts, and in tests. In all of those cases `number()` throws instead of degrading gracefully:

```
RuntimeException: No fallback implementation registered for [Laravel\Prompts\NumberPrompt]
(vendor/laravel/prompts/src/Concerns/Fallback.php:56)
```

This contradicts the documentation, which states that "fallbacks for each prompt have been configured for you." In practice it means a command using `number()` cannot run on Windows and cannot be tested with `expectsQuestion()`.

### Steps To Reproduce

Given a command that uses `number()`:

```php
public function handle()
{
    $count = number('How many people?');

    $this->line("There are {$count} people.");
}
```

Test it (or simply run it on Windows / a non-interactive shell):

```php
$this->artisan('your:command')
     ->expectsQuestion('How many people?', 5)
     ->expectsOutput('There are 5 people.');
```

Expected: the fallback asks the question and returns the number, like every other prompt type.

Actual: it errors with `RuntimeException: No fallback implementation registered for [Laravel\Prompts\NumberPrompt]`.

issue.title: [13.x] Queue workers crash-loop on Redis Cluster / ElastiCache Serverless: cross-slot MGET in getPausedQueues() → TypeError in PhpRedisConnection::mget()
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.25.0

### PHP Version

8.4

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

After upgrading to v13.25.0, every `queue:work` poll iteration throws:

```
TypeError: array_map(): Argument #2 ($array) must be of type array, false given
at vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Redis/Connections/PhpRedisConnection.php:67
```

The exception is thrown inside `Worker::getNextJob()` **before a job is popped**, is caught by its
`catch (Throwable)` block, the worker sleeps 1s and retries — and fails again, forever. The net
effect is that queue workers stop consuming jobs almost entirely (we saw this take down all
production queues; cache/queue backend is AWS ElastiCache **Serverless** Valkey 7.2, which
enforces Redis Cluster semantics).

**The chain:**

1. #61126 (shipped in v13.25.0, "Add a global pause switch for queues") changed
   `QueueManager::getPausedQueues()` to fetch a **global** pause key alongside the per-queue keys:

   ```php
   $keys = array_map(fn ($queue) => "illuminate:queue:paused:{$connection}:{$queue}", $queues);

   $states = $this->app['cache']
       ->store()
       ->many(
           array_merge(['illuminate:queues:paused'], $keys)
       );
   ```

2. On a Redis cache store this becomes a **multi-key `MGET`**. On any cluster-semantics Redis
   (Redis Cluster, ElastiCache Serverless, Valkey serverless), `illuminate:queues:paused` and
   `illuminate:queue:paused:{connection}:{queue}` hash to different slots, so the server replies
   `CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot` — on **every single worker loop**.

3. phpredis signals command error replies by returning `false` (no exception), so
   `PhpRedisConnection::mget()` does `array_map($closure, false)` → `TypeError`. The real
   `CROSSSLOT` error is swallowed (`getLastError()` is never surfaced), which made this
   painful to diagnose.

Notes:

- #60109 (v13.24.0) introduced the `many()` batching for the pause check. That could already
  cross-slot for a worker polling multiple queues (`--queue=a,b`), but the unconditional global
  key in v13.25.0 makes even **single-queue workers** fail 100% of the time.
- `RedisStore::many()` special-cases `PredisClusterConnection` and falls back to `manyAlias()`
  (per-key gets), but there is no equivalent handling for phpredis — and none is possible via
  connection type when the endpoint enforces cluster semantics behind a single proxy endpoint
  (ElastiCache Serverless is used with the regular non-cluster phpredis client).


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Point `CACHE_DRIVER=redis` and `QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis` at any cluster-semantics Redis
   (Redis Cluster, or AWS ElastiCache Serverless Redis/Valkey) using phpredis.
2. Run `php artisan queue:work`.
3. Every poll iteration logs the `TypeError` above and no jobs are consumed.

Minimal reproduction without a worker:

```php
Cache::many(['illuminate:queues:paused', 'illuminate:queue:paused:redis:{default}']);
// TypeError: array_map(): Argument #2 ($array) must be of type array, false given
```

Truncated trace:

```
#0 .../Redis/Connections/PhpRedisConnection.php(67): array_map(Object(Closure), false)
#1 .../Cache/RedisStore.php(112): PhpRedisConnection->mget(Array)
#2 .../Cache/Repository.php(167): RedisStore->many(Array)
#3 .../Queue/QueueManager.php(335): Repository->many(Array)
#4 .../Queue/Worker.php(489): QueueManager->getPausedQueues('redis', Array)
#5 .../Queue/Worker.php(450): Worker->getPausedQueues('redis', Array)
#6 .../Queue/Worker.php(243): Worker->getNextJob(Object(RedisQueue), '{default}')
```

### Expected behavior / suggested fixes

Any of these would have prevented the outage, and they're complementary:

1. **Fail open:** a failure while checking pause state should not prevent job consumption —
   wrap the pause lookup so workers keep processing when the cache read fails.
2. **Cross-slot-safe lookup:** fetch the global key separately from the per-queue keys (or fall
   back to per-key `get`s à la `manyAlias()` when `MGET` fails), so cluster deployments work.
3. **Don't swallow the Redis error:** `PhpRedisConnection::mget()` should detect `false` and
   throw a `RedisException` including `getLastError()` instead of a bare `TypeError` from
   `array_map()`.

### Workarounds

- Pin `laravel/framework` to `~13.24.0` (sufficient for single-queue workers), or
- `Queue::withoutInterruptionPolling()` in a service provider (disables pause *and* restart polling).

issue.title: `route:cache` mutates live route instances, breaking subsequent `optimize` tasks that analyze routes
issue.body: ### Laravel Version 13.19.0 ### PHP Version 8.4.23 ### Database Driver & Version N/A (not database-related) ### Description `RouteCacheCommand` calls `prepareForSerialization()` directly on route instances returned from `getFreshApplicationRoutes()`. https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/3093ff3a61f88225f16fec35dda65e1e7c0867a4/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Console/RouteCacheCommand.php#L56-L64 `Route::prepareForSerialization()` intentionally removes runtime dependencies: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/3093ff3a61f88225f16fec35dda65e1e7c0867a4/src/Illuminate/Routing/Route.php#L1560 Those route objects remain referenced by the live router collection. Later in the same PHP process, any code that still needs to analyze routes can fail with: ``` LogicException: Route is not bound. ``` This happens because after `container` is unset. Access like `$route->container` goes through `__get()`: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/3093ff3a61f88225f16fec35dda65e1e7c0867a4/src/Illuminate/Routing/Route.php#L1569-L1573 which calls `parameters()`: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/3093ff3a61f88225f16fec35dda65e1e7c0867a4/src/Illuminate/Routing/Route.php#L432-L435 And that throws when the route was never bound to a request: https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/3093ff3a61f88225f16fec35dda65e1e7c0867a4/src/Illuminate/Routing/Route.php#L483-L490 This is especially visible with `php artisan optimize`, which runs built-in cache commands before `ServiceProvider::$optimizeCommands`: ```php [ 'config' => 'config:cache', 'events' => 'event:cache', 'routes' => 'route:cache', 'views' => 'view:cache', ...ServiceProvider::$optimizeCommands, ] ``` If a package registers an optimize task that analyzes routes (for example, to cache generated metadata), that task can fail after `route:cache` has already run in the same `optimize` command. ### Steps To Reproduce **Reproduction repository:** https://github.com/hosni-labs/laravel-optimize-command-bug 1. Clone the reproduction repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/hosni/laravel-optimize-command-bug.git cd laravel-optimize-command-bug composer install cp .env.example .env php artisan key:generate ``` 2. The app registers a custom optimize command via `AppServiceProvider`: ```php $this->optimizes( optimize: 'test:route-analysis', key: 'route-analysis', ); ``` 3. The `test:route-analysis` command iterates all routes and analyzes them: ```php foreach (Route::getRoutes() as $route) { dump($route->uri(), $route->getController(), $route->gatherMiddleware()); } ``` 4. Run the command directly — it succeeds: ```bash php artisan test:route-analysis ``` 5. Run it as part of `optimize` — it fails: ```bash php artisan optimize ``` **Expected:** `optimize` completes successfully, including the `route-analysis` task. **Actual:** The `route-analysis` task fails with: ``` LogicException: Route is not bound. ``` The failure occurs on any route when `gatherMiddleware()` is called after `route:cache` has already executed in the same process. **Workaround:** ```bash php artisan optimize --except=route-analysis php artisan test:route-analysis ``` **Proposed fix:** Clone each route before calling `prepareForSerialization()`, and build the route cache file from the cloned/prepared collection so live route instances are not mutated.

issue.title: Accessors receive null when added to appends and toArray is called
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.23.0

### PHP Version

8.5

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

When a model has an accessor for a field and uses the fields value regular functionality works as expected.
Until this attribute is added to the appends, then getting it "normally" `->attributeName` works fine, however calling toArray on the model forces the value passed to the accessor to be null.
This is due to:
https://github.com/laravel/framework/blob/f374d48bc97144bf2ed6e76b1fa2743e615ad446/src/Illuminate/Database/Eloquent/Concerns/HasAttributes.php#L249
having null as it's second parameter

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a model with e.g. price as a database field
2. test if `$model->price` returns the price and if `$model->toArray()['price']` returns the same price
3. Now add an accessor for that price, and add it to the appends
```php
protected $appends = ['price'];

protected function price(): Attribute
{
    return Attribute::get(fn($price) => $price);
}
```
4. test if `$model->price` returns the price and if `$model->toArray()['price']` returns the same price
5. Observe that `$model->toArray()['price']` is now suddenly null instead of the value of `$model->price`

The reason why one would want to add an existing attribute to the appends is that `->toArray()` does not execute the accessors unless they are in the appends.

issue.title: Concurrent parallel test runs fail on the shared compiled view directory
issue.body:
### Laravel Version

13.34.0 (also present on `13.x` at d6e9b9a7d8)

### PHP Version

8.4.20

### Database Driver & Version

_No response_

### Description

`Illuminate\Testing\Concerns\TestViews` gives each parallel worker its own compiled view directory by appending `ParallelTesting::token()`. The token is the worker index, 1 to N, so it is the same in every parallel run. It isolates workers within a run, but two parallel runs of the same project at the same time use the same `test_1`, `test_2`, ... directories.

Both process callbacks that manage that directory fail when another run touches it at the same moment:

```php
ParallelTesting::setUpProcess(fn () => File::ensureDirectoryExists($path));
ParallelTesting::tearDownProcess(fn () => File::deleteDirectory($path));
```

- `ensureDirectoryExists()` checks `isDirectory()` and then calls `makeDirectory()` without `$force`, so it reaches the unsuppressed `mkdir()`. If the other run creates the directory in between, this run fails with `mkdir(): File exists`.
- `deleteDirectory()` checks `isDirectory()` and then constructs a `FilesystemIterator`, which throws `UnexpectedValueException` if the other run removed the directory in between.

Either way, the losing run fails before or after its tests, although nothing in the tests is wrong. It shows up when two parallel runs share a checkout, for example a developer's run beside a local CI job, or two terminals.

The trace from the losing run:

```
mkdir(): File exists
  at Illuminate/Filesystem/Filesystem.php:662
  Illuminate\Filesystem\Filesystem->makeDirectory() at Filesystem.php:643
  Illuminate\Filesystem\Filesystem->ensureDirectoryExists() at Facade.php:364
  Illuminate\Support\Facades\Facade::__callStatic() at Testing/Concerns/TestViews.php:26
```

### Steps To Reproduce

In any application with a parallel-capable test suite, start two parallel runs in the same directory at the same time:

```bash
php artisan test --parallel &
php artisan test --parallel &
wait
```

It is timing-dependent, so it may take a few attempts. The window is widest with many workers and a short suite. The deterministic version is the test added in #61786, which forces each check to see the state from just before the other run acted.

issue.title: maxRelationshipDepth(0) doesn't limit includes at all, and throws on a three-segment path
issue.body:
- Laravel version: 13.24.0
- PHP version: 8.5.9
- Database driver & version: SQLite 3 in memory, through Testbench 11.1

I went looking at JsonApiResource::$maxRelationshipDepth in the source and ended up with a test, because zero turns out to be looser than one rather than stricter.

With maxRelationshipDepth(0), GET /posts/1?include=comments.author comes back byte-identical to the default depth of 5: comments and authors both in included, 3 queries. At depth 1 the nested level is dropped, only comments, 2 queries. So the limit isn't applied at zero at all.

With a three-segment path it stops being a quiet difference. The same setup at depth 0 with ?include=comments.author.comments gives me RelationNotFoundException, "Call to undefined relationship [comments] on model [...\Comment]", after 2 queries and before any query for the third level. Depth 2 and depth 5 both return 200 with comments and authors included, so zero is the only value that breaks.

Where it comes from, as far as I can tell. The setter allows zero on purpose:

    static::$maxRelationshipDepth = max(0, $depth);

and JsonApiRequest::sparseIncluded() is the only place the value is read, minus one:

    $item = implode('.', Arr::take(explode('.', $item), JsonApiResource::$maxRelationshipDepth - 1));

At depth 0 that's Arr::take($segments, -1), and Arr::take() with a negative limit returns the tail, array_slice($array, $limit, abs($limit)), not an empty array. So comments.author keeps author and the nested level loads anyway, and comments.author.comments becomes ['comments'], which goes into loadMissing() on a collection of Comment models that has no comments relation. Checked the helper on its own too: Arr::take(['author', 'comments'], -1) is ['comments'], and with 0 it's [].

What I'm not sure about is what zero is meant to mean, and I'd rather ask than pick. If it means the same as one, no nested includes, then clamping the limit in sparseIncluded() to max(0, $maxRelationshipDepth - 1) is one line and nothing else moves. If zero is meant to be an invalid argument, then max(1, $depth) in the setter is smaller still, but it quietly rewrites what the caller passed, which I like less. What zero can't mean, unless I'm misreading it, is "include nothing at all" — sparseIncluded() with no argument returns array_keys() and never sees the limit, so the first segment gets through at any depth.

Can open a PR with the failing test plus whichever of the two you'd prefer.

Steps to reproduce

Post hasMany Comment, Comment belongsTo Author. Resources generated with make:resource --json-api, PostResource declaring $relationships = ['comments' => CommentResource::class] and CommentResource declaring $relationships = ['author' => AuthorResource::class].

One post with three comments, each comment with an author. Call JsonApiResource::maxRelationshipDepth(0) in setup, then GET /posts/1?include=comments.author.comments with Accept: application/vnd.api+json. For the first half, the same with ?include=comments.author at depths 0, 1 and 5, comparing included and the query count.
